name: WhisperFusion
description: Collabora's ultra-low-latency conversational AI stack chaining WhisperLive (STT) + an LLM (Mistral/Phi via TensorRT-LLM) + WhisperSpeech (TTS) behind a Docker Compose deployment with a served Web GUI. Provides a browser-accessible full-duplex speech conversation demo. No built-in authentication by default; the web GUI is served as HTML on port 8000 with a WhisperLive WebSocket backend behind it.
auth_notes: No authentication in the reference Docker Compose deployment. A simple web server serves the conversational Web GUI on http://<host>:8000 (HTML, so partially Shodan http.html-visible), which then connects to the WhisperLive WebSocket backend for streaming STT and to the TensorRT-LLM + WhisperSpeech pipeline. Neither the GUI nor the WebSocket backend enforces any credential. Because the GUI is minimal (demo frontend, often JS-driven), some markers render in served HTML while the speech transport itself is WebSocket/wire-only.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Direct project-name match in the served Web GUI HTML title/body; high signal where the demo frontend labels itself
WhisperSpeech (the TTS component, near-unique to this Collabora stack) co-occurring with a whisper marker in the demo GUI distinguishes WhisperFusion from generic whisper web UIs
Project name plus the Collabora attribution string in the demo GUI is very high precision and low volume

api_paths: WS (WhisperLive STT backend handshake, JSON config + PCM audio)
known_vulns: No built-in auth — unauthenticated access to a full STT+LLM+TTS conversational pipeline on GPU
LLM prompt-injection / abuse surface — the exposed conversational bridge lets any visitor drive the Mistral/Phi model (jailbreak, content generation, resource abuse) at operator cost
GPU compute theft — the pipeline requires >=24GB GPU RAM; an open instance is high-value free inference (STT + LLM + TTS combined)
WhisperLive WebSocket backend inherits WhisperLive's no-auth, client-selectable-model, plaintext-ws issues
No rate limiting on the conversational endpoint — automatable abuse of the full pipeline
Demo frontend served without TLS or access control in the reference compose file
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) Free conversational-AI compute — an exposed instance chains STT+LLM+TTS on a 24GB+ GPU with no auth; an attacker gets a complete voice-LLM pipeline at operator expense. (2) LLM abuse via the speech/text bridge — driving the backing Mistral/Phi model for prohibited generation or as an open proxy. (3) Audio PII + conversation exfiltration — full-duplex conversations processed with no auth or logging. (4) Chained WhisperLive weaknesses — the STT backend's VRAM-exhaustion and plaintext-ws exposures apply. Deployments are typically demos/research, so hardening is rare.
deployment_notes: Docker Compose reference deployment with pre-built TensorRT-LLM containers; requires a high-VRAM NVIDIA GPU (RTX 4090-class, >=24GB). Web GUI served on 8000 (HTML — partially Shodan http.html-visible); TensorRT/build tooling sometimes exposes 6006. Components: WhisperLive (STT) + Mistral or Phi-2/Phi-3-mini (LLM, TensorRT-LLM) + WhisperSpeech (TTS). The speech transport rides the WhisperLive WebSocket, so deep transport fingerprinting overlaps the WhisperLive profile (Censys/active-probe). Basic host discovery is possible via the served GUI HTML on 8000. Almost always deployed as an unauthenticated demo; enterprise fronting is uncommon.
